Hrasvaroma.note: King of Videha; father of Janaka and Kushadhvaja. The Janaka kings descend from Nimi, a son of Ikshvaku.

people.Janaka: Siradhvaja, the Janaka of the Ramayana. Ploughing the sacrificial ground he turned up Sita from the furrow, sira, and took her as his daughter. SB 9.13.18-19

Kushadhvaja.note: Younger brother of Janaka, king of Sankashya.

Sita.note: Found by Janaka in a furrow of the earth (Bhumija) and raised as his daughter; wife of Rama, carried off by Ravana, at last taken back into the earth. Her birth lineage is none but the Earth's. By name — won at her svayamvara when Rama alone bent and broke Shiva's bow, fourteen years' exile at her own insistence, drawn by the illusion of a golden deer and abducted by Ravana while Rama and Lakshmana were lured away, a year captive in Lanka's Ashoka grove refusing him, found by Hanuman, freed after the war and made to prove her purity by fire (agni-pariksha), exiled again in Ayodhya on a washerman's rumour while pregnant, raising Lava and Kusha alone at Valmiki's ashram, and at their reunion with Rama choosing to return into the earth that bore her rather than prove herself again.

Urmila.note: Daughter of Janaka and Sunayana; wife of Lakshmana, who slept fourteen years in her stead so he could guard Rama night and day.

Mandavi.note: Daughter of Kushadhvaja; wife of Bharata.

ShrutakirtiR.name: Shrutakirti
ShrutakirtiR.note: Daughter of Kushadhvaja; wife of Shatrughna.

MithiJanaka.name: Janaka (Mithi)
MithiJanaka.note: Born of no womb, from the churning of his father's body: hence Vaideha, the bodiless-born, and Mithi, the churned, and Mithila for the city he founded. Every king of this line is called Janaka after him. SB 9.13.12-13

DevarataV.name: Devarata
DevarataV.note: Not Shunahshepha, whom Vishvamitra adopted under the same name. SB 9.13.14

MaruV.name: Maru
MaruV.note: Not Maru of Kalapa in the Ikshvaku line. SB 9.13.15

people.Keshidhvaja: A self-realized king; his cousin Khandikya was expert in ritual, and the two exchanged what each lacked. SB 9.13.21-22
people.Khandikya: Son of Mitadhvaja, master of ritual, who fled Keshidhvaja and later taught him karma-kanda in exchange for knowledge of the self. SB 9.13.22
